newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares close up on limited foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares close up on limited foreign buying.

text.p: Jakarta share prices closed higher on Friday on the back of limited foreign-buying of selected big-capitalised stocks and active second-liners, brokers said.

The Jakarta Composite Index rose 2.57 points, or 0.47 percent, to close at 549.04 points after touching a low of 546.27 points in midsession. Gainers led losers by 63 to 41, with 43 counters unchanged.
One foreign broker said some foreigners were shifting their portfolios and targeting selected big-capitalised stocks as prevailing prices were considered cheap.
"Foreign buyers remain very selective as they await further indications on U.S. interest rate moves," another said.
Textile firm Apac Centertex topped the active list on turnover of 16.8 million shares, rising 25 rupiah to 975 on what brokers said was speculative interest.
Tyre producer Gajah Tunggal rose 75 rupiah to 1,175 on a volume of 13.3 million shares following its August announcement of a rights issue.
Bank Mashill and Bank Tiara were actively traded on speculative interest following a media report that the two had submitted a merger proposal to the central bank.
Bank Tiara rose 250 rupiah to 2,550 rupiah on a turnover of 4.4 million shares. Bank Mashill fell 75 rupiah 2,275 on 3.9 million shares.
Pharmaceutical firm Kalbe Farma rose 250 rupiah to 5,125 rupiah on a turnover of 1.3 million shares.
Brokers said it was actively traded following a "buy" recommendation by a security's report on prospects of higher earnings coupled with market talk of a possible rights issue.
Blue-chips Indosat, Sampoerna and Gudang Garam were among the targets of foreign-buying. Indosat rose 175 rupiah, or 2.33 percent, to 7,675 rupiah on a volume of 575,000 shares.
